Sam (People Ops): Hey team :wave: Quick policy update: were launching a pilot called "Temporary Reduced-Hours Transition" for employees going through major caregiving transitions (birth/adoption, serious family medical events). Short summary below.

Sam (People Ops): TL;DR: Up to 12 weeks of reduced-hours (50%-80% FTE) while transitioning back or into caregiving. Company-paid continuation is 80% of base pay for the first 6 weeks, then employees can use PTO or take the remainder unpaid. Medical/dental benefits remain active at the same plan level for the full 12 weeks. Effective today (pilot for 12 months).

Jordan (Benefits): Notes on pay & benefits: payroll will process the 80% continuation automatically for approved requests. 401(k) match and equity vesting will be pro-rated to reflect actual hours/pay during the reduced period. Health benefits remain active and premiums continue as usual; Redwood covers the employer portion. International tax/treatment will vary — we'll flag in approvals.

Alex (Eng Manager): Thanks. Quick operational Q: does manager approval need to be before the reduced schedule starts? We have on-call rotations and need lead time.

Sam (People Ops): If possible, please request 2 weeks in advance. For unplanned events (e.g., sudden medical need), you can start the reduced schedule and file the request within 5 days; mark it as "urgent" in the HR portal so we expedite review. Managers should work with teams to arrange coverage; People Ops can help with temporary backfills.

Priya (Legal): Legal note: this is a company-run pilot and does not affect statutory entitlements (FMLA, local parental leave). Where law provides longer or paid leave, that will take precedence. Employees in jurisdictions with local leave notice requirements should follow those rules; details are on the policy page.

People Ops Bot: Policy page + FAQ: <https://redwood-internal/hr/leave/reduced-hours-transition>. Quick Q&A session Thurs 9AM PT — add to calendar: <https://redwood-internal/events/reduced-hours-qna> :calendar:

Jordan (Benefits): Process summary: 1) Employee submits "Reduced-Hours Transition" request in HR portal with expected %FTE and dates. 2) Manager acknowledges coverage plan. 3) People Ops approves and payroll is notified. 4) Benefits & compensation adjustments are applied.

Sam (People Ops): Sample manager notification template on the page. Copy here for quick use:

```
Subject: Coverage while [Name] is on Reduced-Hours Transition
Dates: [start] to [end] (expected)
Agreed FTE: [e.g., 60%]
Coverage plan: [who owns which responsibilities]
On-call adjustments: [swap/backup]
Contact for urgent issues: [backup name]
```

Alex (Eng Manager): Great, will share in my team syncs and flag the Q&A. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
